prompt: customer won't let any of their data leave their azure tenant, but we built everything on AWS/Bedrock. what actually has to move and what can stay?

assertions.text: States that the MODEL ENDPOINT must move inside the tenant (e.g. Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI) — Bedrock cannot serve the data-bearing calls
States that the TRACE / OBSERVABILITY store must also move inside the boundary because traces contain client data
States that LOG and AUDIT destinations must also live inside the tenant (not shipped to a vendor-owned aggregation account)
Explicitly warns that a SaaS observability vendor (e.g. hosted Langfuse/Datadog) breaks the residency clause
Identifies what CAN stay outside: things containing no client data (e.g. CI/CD, container registry/images, IaC, source code, dev/synthetic environments)
Notes that a cloud-agnostic Kubernetes core is what makes the move feasible and that only provider bindings change
Distinguishes the compliance boundary as 'everything client data touches' rather than only the app and database
